newsitem.title: USA: Ohio DOT confident can sell more bonds in FY '99.
newsitem.headline: Ohio DOT confident can sell more bonds in FY '99.

text.p: Ohio Department of Transportation announced Wednesday that cost cutting and new revenues will allow issuance of $120 million of highway bonds in fiscal 1999 for new capacity projects and interstate reconstruction.
The department had announced just months ago that fiscal constraints would prevent the issuance of the additional highway bonds approved by voters in a 1995 referendum, spokesman Pieter Wykoff said.

The ballot initiative raised the transportation department's bonding authority from $500 million to $1.2 billion and raised the annual issuance level from $100 million to $220 million over a five-year period, Wykoff said.
Ohio issued $220 million of bonds each of the first two years and anticipates issuing $220 million of bonds backed by the state gasoline tax in fiscal 1998, Wykoff noted.
Cost cutting and new revenues make transportation officials "confident" that they will be able to make the fourth issuance of additional bonds and possibly the fifth, Wykoff said.
